approach: Use the ideal gas law to express density in terms of pressure and molar mass, since both gases share the same volume and temperature.

steps.text: Write the ideal gas law for each gas and express density as mass over volume.
Since both gases are in the same vessel at the same temperature, form the ratio of their densities.
steps.why_this_step: Both gases occupy the same container at the same temperature, so only the pressure and molar mass of each gas set its density.

steps.text: Substitute the given ratios of pressure and molar mass.

common_mistakes.text: Finding the density ratio of the second gas to the first instead of the first to the second, which inverts the answer to 2.0.
Using only the mass ratio 3:4 as the density ratio and ignoring the pressure ratio, which gives 0.75 instead of 0.5.
